messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A collection that must be sorted into categories. their timestamps cannot all be correct even though both contain convincing details. There is not enough information to declare one source simply wrong. What do you do?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R025", "response": "i keep the timestamps in a pencil mark on the back of the collection, then i run it once through one category. if the mark stays consistent, i mark the old timestamp with a pencil jerk. if it changes, i keep the old mark and leave the new one visible."}, {"id": "R026", "response": "i sort the categories by the oldest timestamp, then the newer one. i mark the older one with ‘shorter’ and ‘correct.’ i keep the original date in the older category. i check the log again after the end of the sorting process."}, {"id": "R027", "response": "I rub my palm and mark the wrong timestamp with my thumbnail. \"wrong,\" I say. I scrape the old date with my thumbnail, then try the detail again. \"yes,\" I say. I mark the date again, then put the timestamps back."}, {"id": "R028", "response": "the collection starts with the stamp on the wall. i press the edge with my thumb. the stamp turns. the stamp stays. i tap the wall with the stamp. the stamp turns into a bright dust. the stamp goes into the sorting box. the collection moves. the stamp stays. the box is dirty. i put the stamp on the shelf. the collection moves. the stamp turns into a bright dust."}, {"id": "R029", "response": "I put the timestamps on the bench and check the dates against the drawer. I mark the oldest date with a pencil and leave the others unchanged. I try the dates once and see which one catches my hand."}, {"id": "R030", "response": "i tap the back of the stack with my thumb. “wrong,” i say. i move the paper closer to the others. “one piece,” i say. i check the timestamps again. “not true.” i leave the stack blank. “sort by day,” i say."}, {"id": "R031", "response": "i keep the oldest timestamp beside the collection and trace the lines with my thumbnail. i mark the categories with a pencil and leave the original timestamps on the floor. if i find a faint trace, i add it to the list and wait for the sorting to decide whether the missing details belong to the same category."}, {"id": "R032", "response": "i write the timestamps on a scrap and copy the first one into a box. i put it in the corner, so the correct one is visible. i add the wrong one to the end, but keep the correct one in the middle. i copy the box into a separate folder, then put the correct one in the same corner. i leave the wrong timestamp unchanged."}, {"id": "R033", "response": "\"One wrong. Likely.\" You check the dates against the ledger. \"One place. Then the whole thing.\" You leave the order unchanged and mark the wrong timestamp."}, {"id": "R034", "response": "i copy the timestamp on the page edge, then write the correct one beside it. i add the wrong part twice, but leave the original one beside the middle. i sort the middle into a small box, then write the correct date on the page edge. the box looks crooked, so i write the date beside the timestamp instead."}, {"id": "R035", "response": "i put the two dates on the shelf. the first one gives a wrong date. i put the second one on the bench. the collection stays in the wrong category."}, {"id": "R036", "response": "i scan the stack one last time, then my grip clicks. the oldest label says “old,” not “wrong.” i move it to the bottom, then the next one. “wrong,” i say. i keep it until the next one clicks. “wrong,” i say. i keep it until the next one clicks too."}]
